Motivation:
- Bottleneck: After dynamic-sparse prefill (e.g., MInference) and 3–4b quantization (e.g., SqueezeLLM), single-sequence decode on one GPU is dominated by per-step matmuls and especially full-vocab softmax. Existing accelerators either need a second model (speculative decoding), sacrifice distribution identity (Medusa’s typical acceptance), or mainly help offload regimes (SpecExec). Production stacks also require strict reproducibility and policy fidelity (top-k/p, typical), which typical-accept variants do not guarantee.
- Gaps: We need a single-GPU method that preserves the target model’s output distribution (seed-equivalence), reduces full-vocab work in both verification and correction, adapts online to entropy/penalties/context length, remains robust under 3–4b quantization and long contexts, and certifies compatibility with common sampling policies with exact fallbacks.
- Why now: (1) Segmented/tree attention kernels enable low-overhead per-position verification; (2) 3–4b gather-GEMV microkernels make indexed logit queries cheap; (3) calibration and conformal tools allow conservative, certifiable envelopes; (4) single-GPU inference stacks (vLLM-class) urgently need distribution-identical speedups without extra VRAM.

Methodology:
HydraSpec: identity-preserving self-speculative decoding for single GPUs with two modes: Strict (δ=0, identical distribution) and Conformal (δ>0, near-identity with finite-sample coverage). Novelty over prior work: no second model, certified early-accept gate, softmax-free exact correction via small-support AR, policy-aware certification, and deterministic RNG alignment.

A) Heads and training (identity-respecting self-spec)
- Add K Medusa-style single-layer future-token heads and a skim head to a frozen backbone; tie all heads to the shared output embedding.
- Train heads by teacher forcing on t+1..t+K with KL-to-backbone at temperature Tq. Use label smoothing and spectral-norm regularization to reduce overconfidence. Quantization-aware distillation: compute backbone logits with the exact runtime quantizer and kernels (3–4b) to match deployment numerics.
- Calibrate each head post-hoc via isotonic regression to make top tokens slightly under-confident; export per-head calibration artifacts keyed by model version, bitwidth, rope settings, and kernels.
- Identity-preserving acceptance: use the original speculative rule with q from heads and p from the backbone, applying identical tokenwise warps (temperature, repetition/frequency penalties, banlists) to p and q. Use tree attention with ephemeral KVs for draft nodes and persistent KVs for the accepted prefix; segmented verification kernels minimize recompute.
- Differentiation: unlike speculative decoding, no second model or KV cache; unlike Medusa, no typical-accept; we preserve exact acceptance in Strict mode.

B) Certified early-accept (lossless short-circuit)
- Skim verifier head predicts a conservative lower bound p_lower(x) for the drafted token and a shortlist of alternates.
- Strict mode (δ=0): compute a deployment-specific additive logit error ε (covers quantization + kernel drift). Wrap skim logits with a monotone envelope; set p_lower via softmax(l_hat − ε) on a candidate subset. If q(x_draft) ≤ p_lower(x_draft), accept immediately (guaranteed acceptance under true p). Otherwise verify exactly.
- Conformal mode (δ>0): split-conformal quantile regression on residuals produces p_lower with (1−δ) coverage; track online coverage and auto-tighten if conservative.
- Differentiation: prior self-spec either always verifies p or uses heuristic accept; we provide a certifiable short-circuit.

C) Softmax-free exact correction via small-support acceptance–rejection (AR)
- Target: avoid full-vocab softmax at rejection while sampling exactly from the corrected distribution.
- TailCover proposal r(x): mixture over (i) drafted token, (ii) skim-top-τ, (iii) a small frequent-tokens cache, (iv) a lightweight global tail component with strictly positive mass for all tokens (e.g., unigram-smoothed + tiny uniform ε). Implement O(1) alias sampling over r.
- Pointwise p(x) queries: for sampled x, compute a single-row dot product h·W[x]^T via a 3–4b gather-GEMV kernel with per-row scales/zero-points; apply identical tokenwise warps; no full matmul or softmax.
- Valid AR bounds: precompute per-token logit upper envelopes U(x) using row-norm bounds of W[x] and per-row bias/scale plus a deployment ε; derive a constant M s.t. T(x) ≤ M·r(x) for all x (T is the corrected density). In Strict mode, certify M using conservative norm envelopes and a bound on tail mass from U; in Conformal mode, use a high-quantile M with online monitoring. If AR exceeds B trials at a step, fall back to exact softmax to bound tail latency and preserve identity.
- Differentiation: Medusa/self-spec variants correct with a full softmax; we keep exactness while replacing it with a few indexed dot products and a provable AR bound over a proposal that covers the entire vocabulary.

D) Policy-aware certification with exact fallback
- Tokenwise-separable policies (temperature, additive repetition/frequency penalties, banlists) are identity-preserving by construction.
- Top-k: certify C by proving U(x) < kth(C) for all x ∉ C using per-token U(x); otherwise fall back to a full pass for that step.
- Top-p: prove Σ_{x∈C} L(x) ≥ p or Σ_{x∉C} U(x) ≤ 1−p with log-sum-exp envelopes L/U; otherwise fall back.
- Typical sampling: bound surprise of unseen tokens to prove they cannot enter the typical set; otherwise fall back.
- Differentiation: prior work does not provide policy-level certificates with selective fallback.

E) Per-step adaptive drafting via an identity-aware bandit
- Actions: draft depth γ∈{1..K}, tree shape, skim on/off, shortlist τ, AR budget B.
- Features: entropy H(q), skim-based entropy proxy for p, rolling acceptance and AR success rates, remaining length prediction, GPU occupancy/KV residency, quantization level, long-context flag.
- Reward: tokens/sec minus penalties for AR retries, escalations, and tail latency; slight penalty for probe-based logprob gaps. Doubling-interval updates for rapid within-sequence adaptation.
- Differentiation: unlike Chanakya/APR/SSH (batch/pipeline), this controls speculative micro-decisions within a single sequence and is identity-aware (backs off when certification fails).

F) Quantization- and long-context-aware engineering
- Heads in FP16, backbone in 3–4b. All calibrations (ε, M, policy envelopes) computed with the deployed kernels to avoid train–deploy mismatch.
- Precompute and store compact per-token statistics: 2-byte l2 row-norms and bias bounds for U/L envelopes; negligible VRAM (<1 MB for 128k vocab).
- Prefill uses dynamic sparse attention (e.g., MInference); decoding uses HydraSpec with tree attention and vectorized ephemeral KV buffers; lazy materialize accepted prefixes to keep memory flat at 8k–128k.

G) Determinism and safety
- Deterministic RNG ledger: reserve a fixed number of RNG draws per step and recycle unused ones so the RNG stream is independent of early-accept/AR outcomes; guarantee seed equality with sequential decoding.
- Fallbacks guarantee distribution identity in Strict mode. Conformal mode logs coverage and auto-corrects when over-conservative.
- Property-based tests: bitwise token equality across policies; certification/fallback behavior; tail-latency boundedness via AR budget histograms.

H) Implementation plan (vLLM-class stacks)
- Add K future heads + skim head; export calibration artifacts.
- CUDA kernels: gather-GEMV for 3–4b row queries, warp-specialized dequant on selected rows; segmented/tree attention; alias sampler; partial-normalizer envelopes; CUDA graph capture of verification/correction micrographs.
- Certification hooks for top-k/p/typical; bandit controller; deterministic RNG ledger.
- Calibration set: 20–50k tokens spanning entropy/penalties/context-length buckets to fit ε, M, and policy envelopes; artifacts keyed by model+quantizer+kernel.

How it differs from prior work
- Speculative Decoding: no second model or extra KV cache; we preserve identical distribution in Strict mode and introduce certified early-accept plus softmax-free exact correction.
- Medusa: uses Medusa-style heads but restores the original acceptance rule; adds certification and small-support AR correction to maintain identity; adds strict RNG alignment.
- SpecExec: targets in-memory, single-GPU decoding rather than offload; avoids large deterministic trees; emphasizes certified shortcuts and softmax avoidance.
- SqueezeLLM: orthogonal quantization; we add quantization-aware calibration and gather-GEMV kernels for exact per-row queries.
- Chanakya/APR/SSH: our bandit is per-token, single-sequence, identity-aware, not batch scheduling.

Evaluation plan (to de-risk and quantify gains)
- Models: Llama-3/3.1 8B–13B, Q3/Q4, context 8k–128k.
- Workloads: chat, code completion, long-form summarization; penalties on/off.
- Metrics: speedup vs sequential (tokens/sec), fraction of steps avoiding full softmax, average AR queries per correction, early-accept rate, acceptance depth distribution, fallbacks per 1k tokens, tail-latency p95/p99, VRAM overhead, exactness (bitwise output equality under Strict mode) and policy coverage rate (certified steps share) under top-k/p/typical.
- Ablations: heads K, skim on/off, AR budget B, TailCover components, conformal δ, bandit vs fixed γ, quantization bits, long-context.

Expected impact:
- Throughput/latency: 2.5–4.0x single-sequence speedup on 8B–13B models with 3–4b quant across 8k–128k contexts, with >80% steps avoiding full-vocab softmax in low-entropy spans; bounded tail latency via AR budgets and certified fallbacks.
- Quality/reproducibility: Strict mode preserves exact distribution and seed equality for standard policies; policy-aware certification with exact fallback when proofs fail. Conformal mode offers tunable near-identity with coverage guarantees.
- Robustness/deployability: Adapts online to entropy, penalties, and context; no second model; <0.5% param overhead for heads; integrates with vLLM-like stacks and dynamic-sparse prefill; works under 3–4b quantization on consumer GPUs.
- Generality: Certified early-accept and softmax-free correction extend to encoder–decoder and multimodal models; the calibration/envelope toolkit provides a template for future identity-preserving accelerators.

experimental_design.experiment_strategy:
Three complementary experiments designed for single-GPU Python implementations to validate HydraSpec’s effectiveness and strengths. Each includes setup, metrics, procedures, ablations, and success criteria, plus an executable-style pseudo-code harness that can be adapted for PyTorch/Transformers.

----------------------------------------------------------------
Experiment 1: Strict-mode identity and speed vs. sequential baseline
----------------------------------------------------------------
Goal/Hypothesis
- Demonstrate seed-equivalent distribution (bitwise token equality) under Strict mode across common sampling policies while achieving speedups and avoiding full-vocab softmax on most steps.
- Hypothesis: HydraSpec-Strict maintains bitwise identity with sequential decoding under temperature/penalties/top-k/p/typical policies, with 1.8–3.0x speedup on 8B–13B models (Q3/Q4) and >60% steps avoiding full softmax in low-to-mid entropy spans.

Setup
- Hardware: 1x A100-80GB or RTX 4090 (adjust context length accordingly); CUDA 12.x.
- Software: Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.2+, Transformers, BitsAndBytes (bnb) or AutoAWQ/int4, scikit-learn (for isotonic regression), numpy, einops, tqdm.
- Models: Llama-3/3.1-8B (or 7B) quantized to Q4_K_M (bnb) and Q3_K_M if VRAM permits. Keep lm_head quantized per-row to match deployed numerics.
- Data: 
  - Chat: 2k ShareGPT-style prompts (short/mid, 512–2k tok outputs).
  - Code: 500 HumanEval-like continuations (no eval needed; just generation).
  - Long summarization: 200 Wikipedia long articles (8k–32k ctx), summarize in 1–2k toks.
- Policies: temperature {1.0, 0.7}, repetition/frequency penalties on/off, top-k {0, 40}, top-p {1.0, 0.9}, typical {0, 0.95}. Combine to 8–12 policy configs.

Implementation steps
1) Train Medusa-style heads (K=4–8) + skim head:
   - Freeze backbone. Add K single-layer heads tied to the output embedding; target t+1..t+K teacher forcing with KL-to-backbone @ Tq=1.3–1.7; label smoothing 0.05; spectral-norm regularization.
   - Use 3–5M tokens for quick head training; batch 128; 1–2 epochs.
2) Quantization-aware numerics:
   - Quantize lm_head rows per-row (int4) with stored scales/zeros; dequant path identical to runtime.
   - Compute epsilon: on 50k calibration tokens, measure logit drift between fp16 and quantized row-dot queries and set additive bound ε to 99.9% max drift.
3) Calibration artifacts:
   - For each head, train isotonic regression to convert head logit of top-1 to a calibrated lower bound p_lower; export models.
   - Precompute per-token LM-head row l2 norms and (optional) bias bounds; store as uint16 (2 bytes/token) after scaling.
4) Baseline: Implement sequential decode with deterministic RNG and exact policy application.
5) HydraSpec-Strict: Implement identity-preserving self-spec with certified early-accept and softmax-free AR correction with exact fallback.

Metrics
- Exactness: Bitwise token equality vs. baseline; fraction identical sequences; position-wise mismatch rate (expect 0 under Strict); RNG-stream equality assertion.
- Speed: tokens/sec; average per-step latency; p95/p99 latencies.
- Efficiency internals: fraction of steps avoiding full-vocab softmax; early-accept rate; average AR trials per correction; acceptance depth distribution; fallbacks per 1k tokens.
- Resource: VRAM overhead (heads + stats), GPU utilization.

Procedure
- For each model, dataset, and policy:
  1) Run baseline decode for N prompts (N=100–300 per bucket) with seed s.
  2) Run HydraSpec-Strict with same seed s; assert identity (tokens and RNG ledger equality). If any mismatch, log step and fallback state.
  3) Record speed/latency and internal metrics.
- Context sweep: repeat on contexts 2k/8k/32k/64k (adjust to GPU memory).
- Quantization sweep: Q3 vs Q4.

Ablations
- No-skim vs with-skim (early-accept disabled/enabled).
- AR disabled (force full softmax on correction) vs enabled.
- Heads K ∈ {2, 4, 8}.
- Policy certification on/off (force full softmax under top-k/p/typical) to isolate certification speedups.

Success criteria
- 100% bitwise token equality (all tasks/policies/seeds) in Strict mode.
- ≥1.8x average speedup (end-to-end tokens/sec) on chat/code; ≥1.4x on long summarization at 32k ctx.
- ≥60% steps avoid full softmax in low-entropy spans; early-accept ≥25% on short-answers.
- p95 tail latency within 1.3x of baseline; p99 bounded via AR budget/fallback.

----------------------------------------------------------------
Experiment 2: Early-accept and softmax-free exact correction microbench
----------------------------------------------------------------
Goal/Hypothesis
- Quantify the contribution of (a) certified early-accept and (b) small-support acceptance–rejection (AR) correction to removing full-vocab softmax while preserving exactness.
- Hypothesis: Combined, they eliminate ≥80% of full softmax calls in low-mid entropy; AR requires ≤3.0 indexed row queries on average with bounded p95 under budget B; Strict identity holds.

Setup
- Reuse model/hardware from Exp 1. Focus on one policy suite (temp=1.0, top-k=40, top-p=0.95, penalties off/on).
- Use a balanced 5k-token micro-corpus stratified by token-level entropy bins estimated from q and skim.

Implementation notes
- TailCover r(x): mixture of drafted token, skim top-τ (τ=16–64), frequent-token cache (e.g., top 256 uni-grams), plus tiny uniform ε to ensure full support.
- AR bound M derivation:
  - U(x) = ||h||2 * ||W_row(x)||2 + b_row_max + ε; scale to logits domain including policy warps.
  - Compute conservative global M by bounding tail mass from U(x) versus r(x); in Strict, choose worst-case M; if too loose, clip by budget B and fall back.

Metrics
- Early-accept: fraction of steps short-circuited; false-accepts should be zero in Strict mode (by construction).
- Correction: average and p95 AR trials per corrected step; fraction of steps fully corrected without full softmax; fallbacks due to AR budget exceeded.
- Wallclock: time per accept step vs verify vs correction; total softmax calls avoided.
- Exactness: bitwise equality vs sequential baseline.

Procedure
- Fix a hidden-state capture K=4; run decoding while logging per-step entropy, whether early-accept fired, if correction path used, AR trials count, and whether fallback occurred.
- Compare four variants:
  A) Full HydraSpec (early-accept + AR + certification).
  B) No early-accept (always verify p), AR on.
  C) Early-accept on, AR off (full softmax on rejection).
  D) Both off (always full softmax) — control.
- Sweep τ ∈ {16, 32, 64}, frequent-cache sizes {64, 128, 256}, AR budgets B ∈ {2, 4, 8}.

Success criteria
- Variant A reduces full softmax invocations by ≥70% vs D; ≥40% vs C; ≥50% vs B.
- Mean AR trials ≤3.0; p95 ≤8 with B=8; <2% steps fallback due to AR budget.
- Strict identity holds across all runs.

----------------------------------------------------------------
Experiment 3: Adaptive drafting bandit, policy certification, long-context/quantization robustness
----------------------------------------------------------------
Goal/Hypothesis
- Show online adaptation improves throughput and tail latency across entropy regimes and long contexts, and certify top-k/p/typical steps frequently without full softmax.
- Hypothesis: The identity-aware bandit outperforms fixed γ by ≥10–20% tokens/sec at 32k+ contexts with penalties; certification proves constraints on ≥70% of steps under top-k=40 and ≥50% under top-p=0.9 without fallbacks.

Setup
- Hardware/software/model as in Exp 1. Contexts: 8k, 32k, 64k (adjust for GPU).
- Workloads: mix of chat (variable entropy), code (low entropy), and long summarization (high entropy tail). Include penalty regimes and typical sampling at τ=0.95.

Bandit design (lightweight, implementable)
- Actions: γ ∈ {1, 2, 4, 6}, skim on/off, shortlist τ ∈ {16, 32, 64}, AR budget B ∈ {2, 4, 8}.
- Features per step: entropy H(q) and skim-proxy for p; rolling acceptance rate; AR success rate; context length bucket; quantization bits; KV residency indicator; observed p95 latency over last 128 steps.
- Reward: tokens/sec over last window − 0.1×(AR retries) − 0.5×(fallback) − 0.2×(tail-latency exceed). Update via epsilon-greedy with doubling-interval windows or UCB1 on discretized feature bins.

Policy-aware certification
- Implement certs:
  - Top-k: prove tokens outside C cannot enter top-k using U(x) < kth(C).
  - Top-p: prove Σ L(C) ≥ p or Σ U(¬C) ≤ 1−p using log-sum-exp envelopes.
  - Typical: bound surprise to exclude unseen tokens.
- If proof fails, fall back just for that step (maintains Strict identity).

Metrics
- Throughput: tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency across contexts/policies.
- Certification: certified-step rate per policy; proportion of steps where cert allowed skipping full softmax.
- Bandit behavior: chosen γ distribution, shortlist τ/B adaptations, acceptance depth, fallback rate, AR trials.
- Robustness: results across Q3 vs Q4, 8k vs 64k contexts; VRAM overhead stability.
- Exactness: Strict identity maintained.

Procedure
- Compare: Fixed γ=4 vs bandit; both in Strict mode with certifications enabled.
- For each workload/policy/context/quantization, run ≥100 prompts; plot tokens/sec and latency CDFs.
- Optional: Conformal mode δ ∈ {0.05, 0.10}: measure coverage of early-accept claims and AR-bound M exceed events; track online auto-tightening effects. Also compute empirical TV distance on logits for diagnostics (expect small; identity not required in Conformal).

Success criteria
- Bandit ≥12% throughput gain vs fixed γ at 32k+ ctx; no increase in p99 latency.
- Certification proves constraints on ≥70% steps for top-k=40 and ≥50% for top-p=0.9; typical at ≥40%.
- Strict identity preserved; fallback rate ≤3%.

----------------------------------------------------------------
Appendix: Minimal HydraSpec evaluation harness (Python-like pseudo-code)

Note: This is a blueprint to drop into a PyTorch project. It assumes: (1) K draft heads and a skim head exist, (2) per-token row norms and quantized lm_head rows are prepared, (3) isotonic calibrators and ε/M envelopes are loaded, and (4) policy functions are implemented.

    x = sample_full_softmax(h_t, history, policy_cfg, rng)

- All components are implementable with PyTorch: heads training, isotonic calibration (sklearn), per-row quantization/dequant, gather-row dot via indexed matmul, alias sampling, and envelope checks.
- If Triton is available, gather-row dequant kernels can be added for speed; otherwise prototype in pure PyTorch for correctness and timing.

Risk mitigations
- If calibration ε or M is too loose and hurts speed, AR budget/fallback will cap tail latency while retaining identity. Tighten via more calibration data.

Expected outcomes across experiments
- Strict identity verified across all policies; substantial softmax avoidance with bounded tail latency; bandit improves throughput under long contexts and penalties; certification allows frequent policy-proofed skips of full softmax.
experimental_design.experiment_details:
Below is a complete, implementable plan addressing every item in Experiment Strategy with expanded technical details, reliability enhancements, and code examples suitable for a PyTorch single-GPU setup. All experiments share artifacts (trained heads, calibration, envelopes) to minimize duplication and maximize comparability. Where multiple verification items can be addressed in a single run, we integrate them (e.g., measure exactness, speed, and softmax avoidance together in Experiment 1). We rely on established Python libraries: PyTorch, HuggingFace Transformers, bitsandbytes/AutoAWQ, scikit-learn, numpy, and tqdm. Optional Triton/CUDA Graphs are suggested but not required.

General reproducibility and environment (applies to all experiments)
- Hardware: 1x A100-80GB or RTX 4090. If using 4090, reduce context/sequence lengths accordingly.
- Software: Python 3.10+, CUDA 12.x, PyTorch 2.2+ (with SDP/FlashAttention if available), Transformers ≥4.41, bitsandbytes (bnb) ≥0.42 or AutoAWQ >=0.2.4, scikit-learn ≥1.3, numpy, tqdm.
- Determinism and numerical fidelity:
  - torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
  - torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
  - torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
  - torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False; torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
  - Set all RNG seeds (Python, numpy, torch.cuda.manual_seed_all, torch.manual_seed)
  - Control SDP choice: torch.backends.cuda.enable_flash_sdp(True) only if it is deterministic across runs with same inputs; otherwise disable for Strict-mode runs.
  - Ensure identical tokenization and pre/post-processing by fixing Transformers versions and fast tokenizer flags.
- Dockerfile tip: Start from nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-cudnn8-devel-ubuntu22.04, install miniconda, then pip install pinned versions of torch/transformers/bitsandbytes/sklearn.

Shared artifacts and preparation (one-time for all experiments)
1) Backbone + quantization
- Use Llama-3/3.1-8B–13B. Quantize with bitsandbytes 4-bit (e.g., nf4/int4) or AutoAWQ int4. Freeze backbone weights.
- Tie the LM head to embedding weights if the base model uses weight tying (common for Llama). When using quantization, export a row-wise quantized copy of lm_head with per-row scale and zero-point, preserving the exact runtime dequant path that will be used in HydraSpec. Keep a reference to the dequant function to avoid train–deploy mismatch.

2) Medusa-style future heads and skim head
- Architecture: K single-layer future-token heads that consume h_t and predict t+1..t+K; plus a skim head for lower-bound calibration and shortlist suggestions.
  - Each future head i: LayerNorm(h_t) → GELU MLP (width 4x hidden_size, dropout 0.0) → projection to hidden_size → tie to shared output embedding (via a projection to vocab logits using W_embed^T). Use spectral norm or weight norm on the projection to prevent overconfidence.
  - Skim head: same as future head but outputs logits only for a moderate shortlist size via a top-τ operator during training (for loss efficiency) and full vocab for calibration. Ties to shared embedding as well.
- Training data: 3–5M tokens (mixture of chat/code/wiki). Batch 128, sequence length 1k–2k, gradient accumulation to fit VRAM.
- Loss: For each i in {1..K}, KL(head_i(h_t)/Tq || backbone_softmax_t+i/Tq) with Tq ∈ [1.3, 1.7], plus label smoothing 0.05. Add L2 and spectral-norm regularization on the projection.
- Optimizer: AdamW (lr 1e-4, weight_decay 0.01, betas 0.9/0.95), cosine decay 1–2 epochs. Mixed precision AMP fp16/bf16 for heads; keep backbone frozen.
- Quantization-aware distillation: Compute backbone logits with the exact runtime quantizer for lm_head. For heads, during loss computation, use gather-row dequant queries (see function below) to obtain t+i logits for ground-truth comparison. This matches deploy numerics.

3) Calibration and envelopes (ε, isotonic, per-row stats)
- Epsilon ε (additive logit error bound): On 50k calibration token positions, compute backbone logits using two routes: (a) standard model forward in fp16, (b) gather-row dequant queries mirroring runtime. Record logit drift |ℓ_a − ℓ_b|; set ε = quantile_99.9 over all tokens (or per-token ε_x if storing a vector is feasible). Persist with artifact version hash (model+quantizer+kernel).
- Isotonic calibration for skim head: For each head (and the skim head), collect for the drafted top-1 candidate the pair (q_hat, 1[correct]) or better: map q_head(x_draft) to actual p_backbone(x_draft). Fit sklearn.isotonic.IsotonicRegression with out_of_bounds='clip'. Post-fit, create a conservative lower bound function p_lower = max(isotonic(q), q − m) with small margin m selected by cross-validation to under-confidently bound p. Persist per-head calibrator.
- Per-token row norms and stats: For the lm_head quantized matrix W (vocab_size × hidden_size) compute l2 row norms ||W_x||2 in fp16 (or via dequant of rows in shards) and store as uint16 with a global scale factor. Also store bias bounds if the head has a bias term (many Llama heads have none). This enables U(x) envelopes.
- TailCover caches: Build a small frequent-tokens cache (e.g., top-256 unigram tokens) from a corpus. Persist as int32 indices.

4) Policy warp exactness library
- Implement policy functions with bitwise identity to the baseline reference (Transformers): temperature, repetition/frequency penalty, ban-lists, top-k/p, typical sampling. Validate by unit tests that given the same logits and history, the produced masked/warped logits are numerically identical to a fixed baseline implementation.

5) Deterministic RNG ledger
- Implement an RNG ledger that reserves a fixed number of draws per step (e.g., 16). Unused draws get recycled so the RNG stream is independent of early-accept and AR branch outcomes. This guarantees seed equivalence to sequential decoding.

Reference code snippets (re-usable across experiments)

A) RNG ledger
class RNGLedger:
    def __init__(self, seed: int, draws_per_step: int = 16):
        self.g = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        self.draws_per_step = draws_per_step
        self.buf = []
    def reserve(self) -> float:
        if not self.buf:
            self.buf = list(self.g.random(self.draws_per_step))
        return self.buf.pop(0)
    def recycle_unused(self):
        self.buf = []

B) Quantized gather-row dot for lm_head (int4 per-row)
- Assumes you exported W_int4_packed (uint8) shaped [vocab, hidden//2] with nibbles per element, along with per-row scale s[x] and zero z[x]. Implemented purely in PyTorch for correctness; can be replaced by Triton for speed.

def unpack_int4(packed: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # packed: [m, d//2] uint8, returns int8 values in [0, 15] shape [m, d]
    lo = packed & 0x0F
    hi = (packed >> 4) & 0x0F
    out = torch.empty(packed.shape[0], packed.shape[1] * 2, dtype=torch.int8, device=packed.device)
    out[:, 0::2] = lo.to(torch.int8)
    out[:, 1::2] = hi.to(torch.int8)
    return out

def gather_row_dot(h: torch.Tensor,
                   rows_idx: torch.Tensor,
                   W_packed: torch.Tensor,
                   scale: torch.Tensor,
                   zp: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # h: [H] fp16/fp32; rows_idx: [m]; W_packed: [V, H//2] uint8; scale, zp: [V]
    sel = W_packed.index_select(0, rows_idx)
    sel_int4 = unpack_int4(sel).to(torch.int32)
    # dequant: (val - zp) * scale
    s = scale.index_select(0, rows_idx).unsqueeze(1)
    z = zp.index_select(0, rows_idx).unsqueeze(1).to(torch.int32)
    deq = (sel_int4 - z).to(h.dtype) * s
    # dot per row
    logits = torch.matmul(deq, h)
    return logits  # [m]

C) Policy warp function (temperature, penalties, bans)
- Align with your baseline. Example stub:

def policy_warp(logits: torch.Tensor,
                history: list[int],
                cfg: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
    x = logits.clone()
    if cfg.get('temperature', 1.0) != 1.0:
        x = x / cfg['temperature']
    # repetition penalty (token-wise additive or multiplicative depending on your baseline)
    if cfg.get('repetition_penalty'):
        # implement identically to baseline; e.g., multiplicative penalty per occurred token
        pass
    # frequency/presence penalties
    if cfg.get('frequency_penalty') or cfg.get('presence_penalty'):
        pass
    # banlist: set banned logits to -inf
    if cfg.get('ban'):
        x[cfg['ban']] = -float('inf')
    return x

D) Alias sampler init and draw (numpy for init, torch/numpy for sampling)
class Alias:
    def __init__(self, p: np.ndarray):
        # p must sum to 1 and be strictly positive
        n = len(p)
        q = p * n
        self.prob = np.zeros(n)
        self.alias = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int32)
        small, large = [], []
        for i, qi in enumerate(q):
            (small if qi < 1.0 else large).append(i)
        while small and large:
            s = small.pop()
            l = large.pop()
            self.prob[s] = q[s]
            self.alias[s] = l
            q[l] = q[l] - (1.0 - q[s])
            (small if q[l] < 1.0 else large).append(l)
        for i in large + small:
            self.prob[i] = 1.0
            self.alias[i] = i
    def sample(self, u1: float, u2: float) -> int:
        # u1 in [0,1), u2 in [0,1)
        n = len(self.prob)
        i = int(u1 * n)
        return i if (u2 < self.prob[i]) else self.alias[i]

E) Envelopes U(x) and conservative constant M for AR
- Per step, compute ||h_t||2. Then U_logit(x) = ||h_t||2 * row_norm[x] + b_max + ε. If bias absent, b_max=0. Apply policy warp monotone envelopes (e.g., temperature rescales U). For proposal r(x), compute M = max_x exp(U_logit(x)) / r(x). In practice, compute M over a superset: drafted token, skim shortlist, frequent-cache, plus a global tail bound using a pooled upper bound U_max for the rest with proposal mass r_tail. To avoid O(V) max each step, precompute per-token row_norm and maintain r(x); approximate tail via U_max.

F) Top-k/p/typical certification
- Top-k: Let kth_C be the kth largest warped logit among candidate set C (computed exactly for C). If for all x ∉ C, U_logit(x) < kth_C, then certified; else fallback.
- Top-p: Use unnormalized f(x) = exp(logit(x)). Compute lower bound for C: L_C = sum_{x∈C} exp(L_logit(x)); upper bound for tail: U_tail = sum_{x∉C} exp(U_logit(x)). If L_C / (L_C + U_tail) ≥ p or U_tail / (U_tail + sum_{x∈C} exp(U_logit(x))) ≤ 1-p, certified.
- Typical: For target surprise s* (e.g., mean surprise), bound surprises of unseen tokens using U_logit to ensure they cannot enter the typical set; otherwise fallback.

G) Strict-mode speculative acceptance test (single token)
- Given q (draft) and p (true) under identical warp, accept if x_draft drawn from q is also consistent with original acceptance rule: accept with probability min(1, p(x_draft)/q(x_draft)). In Strict mode we implement original rule, not typical-accept. Early-accept short-circuits when q(x_draft) ≤ p_lower(x_draft) (conservative lower bound guarantees acceptance).


----------------------------------------------------------------
Experiment 1: Strict-mode identity and speed vs. sequential baseline
----------------------------------------------------------------
Goal/Hypothesis
- Verify seed-equivalent distribution (bitwise equality) under Strict mode across policies, while achieving 1.8–3.0x speedup (chat/code) and ≥60% steps avoiding full softmax in low-to-mid entropy.

Setup
- Hardware/Software: as in Shared. Ensure deterministic flags as above.
- Models: Llama-3/3.1-8B or 7B; quantize to Q4_K_M (bnb) and Q3_K_M if VRAM permits. Export lm_head in row-wise int4 with per-row scale/zp (matching runtime). Keep heads in fp16.
- Data: three workloads
  - Chat: 2k ShareGPT-like prompts; 512–2k generated tokens.
  - Code: 500 code completion prompts (HumanEval-like), 256–1k generated tokens.
  - Long summarization: 200 long Wikipedia/article contexts (8k–32k), 1–2k generated tokens.
- Policies: 8–12 configs combining temperature {1.0, 0.7}, top-k {0, 40}, top-p {1.0, 0.9}, typical {0, 0.95}, repetition/frequency penalties on/off.

Implementation steps (artifact production included)
1) Train heads (K=4–8) + skim head as specified above.
2) Quantization-aware numerics and ε: derive ε on 50k calib tokens; store artifacts keyed by model+quantizer+kernel.
3) Isotonic calibration (per head) and per-row stats (row_norms, bias bounds if any), frequent-token cache.
4) Baseline sequential decode: Plain Transformers generation disabled; implement a custom generation loop applying exact policy warp and torch.multinomial sampling for final draw; record RNG draws (random numbers) and final tokens for comparison.
5) HydraSpec-Strict implementation with:
  - K draft heads + skim head; tree attention for verification (use FlashAttention2 segmented kernels if available; otherwise recompute via model forward for the accepted prefix only).
  - Certified early-accept: if q(x_draft) ≤ calibrated p_lower(x_draft) under same policy warp, accept w/o verifying p.
  - Softmax-free correction: AR with TailCover proposal (draft token + skim top-τ + frequent-cache + ε-uniform tail) and strict M from U(x), with fallback to full softmax if AR exceeds budget B.
  - Policy-aware certification hooks for top-k/p/typical; if proof holds, skip full softmax; else fallback path preserves identity.
  - Deterministic RNG ledger as described.

Metrics
- Exactness: fraction of sequences with bitwise equality; position-wise mismatch rate (expect 0); RNG-stream equality check.
- Speed/latency: tokens/sec; average per-step latency; p95/p99 latencies.
- Internals: fraction of steps avoiding full softmax; early-accept rate; AR trials per corrected step (mean, p95); acceptance depth distribution; number of fallbacks per 1k tokens.
- Resource: VRAM overhead (heads + stats); GPU utilization.

Procedure
- For each model, dataset, and policy config:
  1) Baseline decode N prompts (N=100–300) with seed s; store outputs and RNG stream logs.
  2) HydraSpec-Strict with same seed s; assert identity tokens; compare RNG ledgers. Log early-accept, AR trials, and fallbacks.
- Context sweep: contexts 2k/8k/32k/64k; adjust to GPU memory. Quantization sweep: Q3 vs Q4.

Ablations
- No skim vs skim on (early-accept off/on).
- AR disabled (force full softmax on rejection) vs enabled.
- K ∈ {2, 4, 8}.
- Policy certification off (always full softmax) vs on.

Success criteria
- 100% bitwise token equality in Strict mode across all policies.
- ≥1.8x average speedup on chat/code; ≥1.4x on long summarization at 32k.
- ≥60% steps avoid full softmax in low-entropy spans; early-accept ≥25% on short answers.
- p95 ≤ 1.3x baseline; p99 bounded via AR budget/fallback.

Example code skeleton for a Strict step (focus on early-accept + AR)

@torch.no_grad()
def hydraspec_step_strict(h_t: torch.Tensor,
                         history: list[int],
                         artifacts,
                         policy_cfg: dict,
                         rng: RNGLedger,
                         model_ctx) -> tuple[int, dict]:
    # Draft logits (heads consume h_t)
    q_logits_list = [head(h_t) for head in artifacts.future_heads]  # each [V]
    skim_logits = artifacts.skim_head(h_t)  # [V]

    # Draft first token and skim shortlist
    q_warp_0 = policy_warp(q_logits_list[0], history, policy_cfg)
    x_d = int(torch.argmax(q_warp_0))
    shortlist = torch.topk(skim_logits, k=artifacts.skim_topk).indices

    # Calibrate lower bound for acceptance
    q_hat = torch.softmax(q_warp_0, dim=-1)[x_d].item()
    p_lower = artifacts.isotonic[0].predict(np.array([q_hat]))[0]
    # Conservative wrap with epsilon margin
    p_lower = max(p_lower - artifacts.calib_margin, 0.0)

    # Early-accept
    if q_hat <= p_lower:
        rng.recycle_unused()
        return x_d, {"path": "early_accept", "ar_trials": 0, "fallback": False}

    # Exact speculative acceptance: verify p(x_d) on small subset
    need = torch.unique(torch.cat([shortlist, torch.tensor([x_d], device=shortlist.device)])).cpu()
    logits_needed = gather_row_dot(h_t, need, artifacts.W_packed, artifacts.scale, artifacts.zp)
    logits_needed = policy_warp(logits_needed, history, policy_cfg)
    p_needed = torch.softmax(logits_needed, dim=-1)
    idx = (need == x_d).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
    p_xd = p_needed[idx]
    if torch.rand(1).item() <= min(1.0, (p_xd / q_hat).item()):
        rng.recycle_unused()
        return x_d, {"path": "verify_accept", "ar_trials": 0, "fallback": False}

    # AR correction
    # Build TailCover proposal over indices; mix weights
    C = torch.cat([torch.tensor([x_d]), shortlist])
    C = torch.unique(C).cpu().numpy()
    vocab = artifacts.vocab_size
    eps = artifacts.tail_eps
    freq_cache = artifacts.freq_cache  # numpy array
    # proposal masses (unnormalized)
    w_draft = artifacts.w_draft
    w_skim = artifacts.w_skim
    w_freq = artifacts.w_freq
    w_uni = artifacts.w_uni
    r = np.full(vocab, w_uni * eps, dtype=np.float64)
    r[x_d] += w_draft
    r[C] += w_skim / max(1, len(C))
    r[freq_cache] += w_freq / len(freq_cache)
    r /= r.sum()
    alias = Alias(r)

    # Precompute strict M using U(x) envelopes
    h_norm = float(torch.linalg.vector_norm(h_t).item())
    U_logit = h_norm * artifacts.row_norm + artifacts.bias_max + artifacts.epsilon
    # For speed, only compute max over top candidates and bound rest by U_max and r_tail
    candidate = np.unique(np.concatenate([np.array([x_d]), C, freq_cache]))
    M_cand = np.max(np.exp(U_logit[candidate]) / r[candidate])
    non_cand_mask = np.ones(vocab, dtype=bool); non_cand_mask[candidate] = False
    U_max_tail = np.max(U_logit[non_cand_mask]) if non_cand_mask.any() else -1e9
    r_tail = float(r[non_cand_mask].max()) if non_cand_mask.any() else 1.0
    M_tail = np.exp(U_max_tail) / max(r_tail, 1e-12)
    M = max(M_cand, M_tail)

    trials = 0
    while trials < artifacts.AR_budget:
        u1, u2, u3 = rng.reserve(), rng.reserve(), rng.reserve()
        x_prop = alias.sample(u1, u2)
        # Pointwise p via gather-row
        x_tensor = torch.tensor([x_prop], device=h_t.device)
        logit_x = gather_row_dot(h_t, x_tensor, artifacts.W_packed, artifacts.scale, artifacts.zp)[0]
        logit_x = policy_warp(logit_x, history, policy_cfg)
        f_x = torch.exp(logit_x).item()
        a = f_x / (M * r[x_prop])
        if u3 < a:
            rng.recycle_unused()
            return int(x_prop), {"path": "ar_correction", "ar_trials": trials + 1, "fallback": False}
        trials += 1

    # Fallback to exact full softmax
    logits_full = artifacts.full_logits_fn(h_t, history, policy_cfg)  # single full pass
    p_full = torch.softmax(logits_full, dim=-1)
    u = rng.reserve()
    x = int(torch.searchsorted(torch.cumsum(p_full, dim=-1), u * p_full.sum()).item())
    rng.recycle_unused()
    return x, {"path": "fallback_full_softmax", "ar_trials": trials, "fallback": True}


----------------------------------------------------------------
Experiment 2: Early-accept and softmax-free exact correction microbench
----------------------------------------------------------------
Goal/Hypothesis
- Quantify contributions of certified early-accept and AR correction to softmax elimination while preserving Strict identity.
- Hypothesis: Early-accept + AR eliminates ≥80% full softmax calls in low-mid entropy. Mean AR trials ≤3.0 (p95 ≤8 with B=8). Strict identity holds.

Setup
- Reuse model/hardware from Experiment 1. Use a balanced 5k-token micro-corpus stratified by token-level entropy bins (based on q_logits and skim head proxies). Fix one policy suite: temp=1.0, top-k=40, top-p=0.95, penalties off/on.

TailCover and AR implementation details
- TailCover proposal components:
  - Drafted token: mass w_draft (e.g., 0.5)
  - Skim top-τ: distribute mass w_skim across τ tokens uniformly or proportional to calibrated p_lower
  - Frequent-token cache: mass w_freq across 128–256 frequent tokens
  - Uniform tail: w_uni × ε across all tokens (ε small, e.g., 1e-8) to ensure full support
  - Normalize r to sum 1; build Alias(r) once per step.
- AR bound M:
  - Compute U_logit(x) as in Experiment 1 using per-row norms and ε.
  - Compute M = max_x exp(U_logit(x))/r(x). Approximate by max over candidate sets plus a conservative bound for the remaining tail using U_max_tail and max tail mass r_tail.
  - If M is too large (AR success rate drops), the AR budget B and fallback cap tail latency while preserving identity.

Metrics
- Early-accept: fraction of steps short-circuited; by construction, false-accepts are zero in Strict mode.
- Correction: AR trials per corrected step (mean, p95); fraction of corrected steps that avoid full softmax; fallback rate due to AR budget exceed.
- Wallclock: time per accept/verify/correction step; total avoided full softmax calls.
- Exactness: bitwise identity vs sequential baseline.

Procedure
- Implement four variants on the same micro-corpus and log per-step events:
  A) Full HydraSpec: early-accept + AR + policy certification
  B) No early-accept, AR on
  C) Early-accept on, AR off (full softmax on rejection)
  D) Both off (always full softmax) — control
- Sweep τ ∈ {16, 32, 64}, frequent-cache ∈ {64, 128, 256}, AR budget B ∈ {2, 4, 8}. Keep Strict mode.
- For each variant, generate with identical seeds and compare bitwise outputs; log softmax calls avoided and AR stats.

Success criteria
- Variant A reduces full softmax invocations by ≥70% vs D; ≥40% vs C; ≥50% vs B.
- Mean AR trials ≤3.0; p95 ≤8 with B=8; fallback <2% steps.
- Perfect Strict identity across runs.

Example microbench logging hook

----------------------------------------------------------------
Experiment 3: Adaptive drafting bandit, policy certification, long-context/quantization robustness
----------------------------------------------------------------
Goal/Hypothesis
- Demonstrate online adaptation improves throughput and tail latency across entropy regimes and long contexts, and that policy certification can skip full softmax frequently without violating Strict identity.
- Hypothesis: Bandit ≥12% tokens/sec gain vs fixed γ at 32k+ contexts; certification proves constraints on ≥70% steps (top-k=40) and ≥50% (top-p=0.9); Strict identity preserved, fallback ≤3%.

Setup
- Same models and hardware. Contexts: 8k, 32k, 64k (adjust for GPU). Workloads cover chat (variable), code (low entropy), summarization (high entropy tail). Include penalties and typical sampling 0.95.
- Quantization: compare Q3 and Q4.

Bandit controller
- Action space per step: γ ∈ {1, 2, 4, 6}, skim on/off, shortlist τ ∈ {16, 32, 64}, AR budget B ∈ {2, 4, 8}.
- Features per step: entropy H(q) and skim entropy proxy; rolling acceptance rate over last 64 steps; AR success rate over last 64 steps; context bucket (one-hot: 8k/32k/64k); quant bits (Q3/Q4); KV residency flag; observed p95 latency over last 128 steps.
- Reward: instantaneous tokens/sec (smoothed over last 32 steps) − 0.1×(AR retries) − 0.5×(fallback) − 0.2×(tail-latency exceed threshold). Tail threshold can be baseline p95.
- Policy: UCB1 or epsilon-greedy over discretized feature bins. For simplicity and determinism, use epsilon-greedy with epsilon decaying by doubling-interval windows: epsilon = 0.2 for first 64 steps, 0.1 next 128, 0.05 thereafter, reset on large entropy regime changes detected by KL drift in q.
- Identity-awareness: If certification fails repeatedly or AR retries exceed a threshold, automatically reduce γ and increase τ/B conservatively.

Policy-aware certification hooks
- Implement cert functions for top-k, top-p, typical as described above. Use the same per-row U/L envelopes, ε, and log-sum-exp bounds. If proof fails, fallback for that step to exact full softmax (preserves identity). Maintain stats: certification success rate, skip-softmax rate attributable to certification.

Metrics
- Throughput: tokens/sec; p95/p99 latency across contexts/policies.
- Certification: certified-step rate per policy; fraction of steps where cert enabled skipping full softmax.
- Bandit behavior: action distribution (γ, τ, B), acceptance depth, fallback rate, AR trials.
- Robustness: across Q3 vs Q4; 8k vs 64k contexts; VRAM overhead.
- Exactness: Strict identity maintained.

Procedure
- Compare fixed γ=4 vs bandit. Both Strict with certifications enabled. For each workload/policy/context/quantization, run ≥100 prompts; plot tokens/sec and latency CDFs. Also log per-step features and chosen actions for interpretability.
- Optional Conformal mode δ ∈ {0.05, 0.10}: Measure coverage of early-accept claims and AR-bound M exceed events (empirical). Track auto-tightening behavior (reduce δ if over-conservative) and compute empirical TV distance on logits for diagnostics (not required to be zero in Conformal).

Success criteria
- Bandit ≥12% throughput gain vs fixed γ at 32k+ ctx; no increase in p99 latency.
- Certification: ≥70% steps certified for top-k=40; ≥50% for top-p=0.9; typical ≥40%.
- Strict identity preserved; fallback rate ≤3%.

Example bandit code skeleton

class SimpleBandit:
    def __init__(self, actions):
        self.actions = actions  # list of tuples (gamma, skim, tau, B)
        self.counts = np.zeros(len(actions), dtype=np.int32)
        self.values = np.zeros(len(actions), dtype=np.float64)
        self.step = 0
    def select(self, features):
        # epsilon schedule by doubling intervals
        if self.step < 64: eps = 0.2
        elif self.step < 192: eps = 0.1
        else: eps = 0.05
        self.step += 1
        if np.random.rand() < eps:
            return np.random.randint(len(self.actions))
        else:
            return int(np.argmax(self.values))
    def update(self, a_idx, reward):
        self.counts[a_idx] += 1
        n = self.counts[a_idx]
        self.values[a_idx] += (reward - self.values[a_idx]) / n

# Reward computation
class RewardMeter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.lat_hist = []
    def observe(self, step_latency_ms, tokens_out, ar_retries, fallback):
        self.lat_hist.append(step_latency_ms)
        inst_tps = tokens_out / (step_latency_ms / 1000.0)
        penalty = 0.1 * ar_retries + 0.5 * int(fallback) + 0.2 * int(step_latency_ms > np.percentile(self.lat_hist[-128:], 95) if len(self.lat_hist) >= 128 else 0)
        return max(inst_tps - penalty, 0.0)


Reliability enhancements and risk mitigations (applies to all experiments)
- Exactness guardrails:
  - Strict mode always falls back on certification failure or AR budget exceeded. This ensures distribution identity and seed equality.
  - RNG ledger guarantees identical random streams regardless of early-accept or AR outcomes.
- Calibration robustness:
  - If ε or M are loose: increase calibration set to 100k tokens; stratify by entropy, penalties, and context length; recompute envelopes.
  - Track online acceptance coverage in Conformal mode; auto-tighten δ or switch to Strict temporarily if coverage drifts.
- Numerical drift:
  - All per-row queries use the same dequantization path and scales/zero-points as the deployed quantizer (bnb/AWQ). Validate by unit tests comparing a small set of rows to a full matmul slice.
- Tail latency caps:
  - AR budget B guarantees bounded retries; fallback ensures tail latency is bounded. Monitor per-step latency histogram and adapt B via bandit if p95 tails creep.
- Memory:
  - Heads add <0.5% parameters; per-row stats are tiny (<1 MB for 128k vocab). Use vectorized ephemeral KVs for drafted nodes; lazy-materialize accepted prefixes.


Appendix: Minimal end-to-end evaluation harness outline

def decode_sequential(model, prompt_ids, policy_cfg, seed):
    rng = RNGLedger(seed)
    history = []
    outputs = []
    kv = model.init_kv()
    # prefill
    kv, h_t = model.prefill(prompt_ids)
    for t in range(policy_cfg['max_new_tokens']):
        logits = model.forward_last(h_t, kv)  # full vocab logits
        logits = policy_warp(logits, history, policy_cfg)
        p = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        u = rng.reserve()
        x = int(torch.searchsorted(torch.cumsum(p, dim=-1), u * p.sum()).item())
        rng.recycle_unused()
        outputs.append(x)
        history.append(x)
        kv, h_t = model.update_kv(x, kv)
    return outputs

def decode_hydraspec_strict(model, prompt_ids, policy_cfg, seed, artifacts):
    rng = RNGLedger(seed)
    history = []
    logs = []
    outputs = []
    kv = model.init_kv()
    kv, h_t = model.prefill(prompt_ids)
    for step in range(policy_cfg['max_new_tokens']):
        x, info = hydraspec_step_strict(h_t, history, artifacts, policy_cfg, rng, model)
        outputs.append(x)
        history.append(x)
        logs.append(info)
